classification.difficultyReason: Use supplied equal-part models to convert between mixed numbers and improper fractions.

content.prompt: Shade these shapes to represent the given fraction and fill in the boxes.

spec.description: Two unshaded rectangles side by side, each divided into four equal vertical strips.
spec.mathematics: Eight available quarter-parts; the student shades six.
spec.answerVisibility: No shading or completed response appears in the question figure.

answer.short: $\frac{6}{4}$. Shade one whole rectangle and two strips of the second.
answer.worked: Each whole contains 4 quarter-parts. Shade all 4 parts of the first rectangle and 2 parts of the second. There are 6 shaded quarter-parts, so $1\frac{2}{4}=\frac{6}{4}$.

spec.description: One complete rectangle and two of the second rectangle's four strips shaded.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed shading appears only in the solution.

spec.description: Four upright regular pentagons in a horizontal row, each divided from its centre to its vertices into five equal triangular regions.
spec.mathematics: Twenty available fifth-parts; the student shades seventeen.
spec.answerVisibility: No shading or completed response appears in the question figure.

answer.short: $3\frac{2}{5}$. Shade three whole pentagons and two regions of the fourth.
answer.worked: Shade 17 fifth-parts. Group 15 of them into 3 complete pentagons, with 2 fifth-parts left over. Thus $\frac{17}{5}=3\frac{2}{5}$.

spec.description: Three complete pentagons and two of the fourth pentagon's five regions shaded.
spec.mathematics: Seventeen fifth-parts form three wholes and two fifths.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed shading appears only in the solution.

spec.description: Three unshaded circles in a horizontal row, each divided into eight equal sectors.
spec.mathematics: Twenty-four available eighth-parts; the student shades eighteen.
spec.answerVisibility: No shading or completed response appears in the question figure.

answer.short: $\frac{18}{8}$. Shade two whole circles and two sectors of the third.
answer.worked: Each whole contains 8 eighth-parts. Shade all 16 parts of the first two circles and 2 parts of the third. There are 18 shaded eighth-parts, so $2\frac{2}{8}=\frac{18}{8}$.

spec.description: Two complete circles and two adjacent eighth-sectors of the third circle shaded.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed shading appears only in the solution.

spec.description: Four upright isosceles triangles in a horizontal row, each divided from apex to base midpoint into two equal regions.
spec.mathematics: Eight available half-parts; the student shades seven.
spec.answerVisibility: No shading or completed response appears in the question figure.

answer.short: $3\frac{1}{2}$. Shade three whole triangles and one half of the fourth.
answer.worked: Shade 7 half-parts. Group 6 of them into 3 complete triangles, with 1 half left over. Thus $\frac{7}{2}=3\frac{1}{2}$.

spec.description: Three complete triangles and one of the fourth triangle's two halves shaded.
spec.mathematics: Seven half-parts form three wholes and one half.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed shading appears only in the solution.
